title: Probe called for into deaths caused by cops; Public forum set for today
article: Four civilian deaths at the hands of police during August shows that a watchdog is needed more than ever, say B.C. civil libertarians.
"It is a macabre coincidence that there were so many deaths," Murray Mollard, executive director of the B.C. Civil Liberties Association, said yesterday.
"Deaths at the hands of police are not rare events. We want to see continuing public exposure to this issue and exert pressure at the political level."

The association is holding a free public forum today at the Robson Square Theatre in Vancouver from 8:30 a.m. until 1 p.m. Speakers will include relatives of Ian Bush, Kevin St. Arnaud and Gerald Chenery, who died at the hands of police.
Another panelist will be Andre Marin, Ontario ombudsman and a specialist on the subject.
"When police officers investigate other police officers, families do not get any answers," said Sylvia Fee, sister of Chenery, who was shot 13 times by two Vancouver police officers in 2004.
Police said Chenery was threatening them with two steak knives in an alley.
"You can't just kill somebody and expect it to be OK. It could be anybody's brother," said Fee.
"Police take things the wrong way and then bang, you're dead. Police \[investigations\] protect their own interests. Officers are told they did the right thing. They have too much power.
Mollard said investigations should be conducted by a civilian agency.
"In England and Wales, independent police commissions are responsible for investigating deaths," he said.
He called on Solicitor-General John Les and federal Public Safety Minister Stockwell Day to "demonstrate real leadership."
Mollard said he does not believe statistics are kept in B.C. or Canada about the extent of the situation.
B.C. coroners' reports show that 13 civilians died at police hands in 2005 and 11 in 2004, he said.
"No one knows the scope of the problem."
